analysis.title: Energy Natural Resources and Utilities Preview Desk Views Quick Hits on EPS
key_insights: BKR: strong quarter with positive momentum in IET (Industrial & Energy Technology) and OFSE (oilfield services and equipment) broadly in line, which should ease concerns heard into the print about IET rate of change and downside to OFSE.

BKR: IET Horizon 2 order guide is higher, FY guidance is raised (with some Middle East assumptions), and the company highlighted a large generation and cooling order from a major US tech company. Positioning has been lighter over the last couple of weeks but the stock still screens as more owned into the print.

DINO: 3Q adjusted EBITDA of $2.98 bn was well ahead of Street at $2.11 bn, with higher cash flow. RIN / SRE impacts are topical and the size of the beat is debated. A new CEO was announced with the print. DINO was one of the more crowded longs into the print.

OKE: investors are cautious on the path forward. 2026 EBITDA guidance was raised by $200 mn at the midpoint, generally in line with Street, and buyside numbers are expected to already be near $8.6 bn for FY2026. Questions linger on the path to the long-term EBITDA CAGR target.

PUMP: the print was generally in line after a low bar on frac and power. Service revenues were $355 mn vs Street at $317 mn. Focus is on PROPWR: the company points to deploying >500 MW by early 2028 and narrowed capex guidance. With limited MWs left to contract, the open question is how the mix shifts between O&G, Industrial and data center customers.

PSX: results were mixed. Midstream was lighter than expected and Chems was ahead. Refining gross margin per barrel was ahead of Street and the system ran at 98% utilization. Net debt fell from $16.5 bn at 2Q to $12.7 bn at 3Q end, and buybacks plus deleveraging have been well received.

EXE: capex came in hotter for 4Q and 2026 vs Street, consistent with inflationary cost pressures across E&Ps. Production guidance range was revised, in line with Street at the midpoint. Investors do not expect a material change in messaging under the new CEO, whose first earnings call this is.
